$comment: Catalog-level UI builder policy for :remote-catalog, beside its own cover sheet. PER-COMPONENT policy is @BuilderComponent on the sticker, not here. The published catalog and its immutable renderer runtime consume this policy. The three-surface contract is docs/design/REMOTE_M3_UI_BUILDER.md; the generic catalog contract is https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_CATALOG_CONTRACT.md
$comment_catalogId: Not declared, and that is the point: this module's `system` in catalog.spec.json IS `remote-m3`, which is the id the builder has always authored against. 'A builder catalog is a served catalog' holds here by construction, where the sibling :catalog has to declare it — see that module's policy for why.

wasm.reason: The selectable Visual Editor draws Wear Compose CMP stand-ins. The read-only Browser Preview is a separate DEVICE surface: CMP Remote M3 records a real .rc document in Wasm and the pinned CMP RcComposePlayer plays it in each selected host frame. Approximate describes authoring only, never the Browser Preview.

native.reason: The generated creation-DSL Kotlin compiled against this module's own alpha Remote Compose trio and rasterised by the real player — the same lane that produces every sticker in this catalog.

$comment_browserPreview: No browserPreview capability is declared. That legacy capability asks the host/server to compile an RC document and makes the editor bypass the catalog runtime's DEVICE surface. remote-m3 instead owns Browser Preview end to end inside its exact-pinned runtime: CMP/Wasm Remote M3 creation followed by CMP/Wasm RC playback. Native/Live remains the separate authoritative Android lane.

frame.$comment_adapter: Not a screen. A Remote Compose widget is drawn into a host container of a fixed size, so the frame is the host, not a watch face: `frame/widget-host` rather than the sibling catalog's `frame/round-screen`. This is the second reason `remote-m3` is a catalog of its own rather than a mode of the Wear one.

geometry.$comment: The two host sizes are DECLARED BY THE PREVIEW CONTRACT, not measured after the fact: remote-catalog/src/main/kotlin/ee/schimke/wearm3catalog/remote/WidgetContainerPreviews.kt pins @Preview(widthDp = 216, heightDp = 76) and (216, 124), being 200x60dp and 200x108dp of content plus 8dp of padding on every edge. Every widget sticker in this catalog renders at one of them, so they are the sizes a builder must offer. Recorded here rather than transcribed into the server, which carried both numbers as constants.

$comment_composeSourceExport: The Compose source emitter this catalog's designs export through, resolved by the host against the emitters it ships (compose-ui-builder's CatalogExportRouting). `remote-compose` is the Remote Compose screen exporter the builder reaches today for `remote-m3` by its id; declaring it is what lets a catalog-owned `remote-m3` keep offering Kotlin export once that id test is gone.

colorTokens.$comment: The theme roles a colour property may name. Same Material 3 vocabulary as the sibling :catalog, and stated here for the same reason: a Remote design names roles, and a role the canvas cannot resolve is a literal. Every sticker in this catalog is a RemoteDocument carrying explicit dark-first Material colours, so the values behind these names are the document's rather than a theme's — but the names are what a design writes.

menu.$comment: This catalog's own @CatalogComponent(group = …) vocabulary. Widget Container and Scaffold templates lead because a Remote design starts from a container: everything else goes inside one. Selection buttons, Edge-hugging buttons, Sliders and Steppers are declared only in src/snapshot/kotlin and were missing from this list, so under the snapshot lane the builder appended them after every ordered group and sorted them alphabetically - the order a person saw was not the one stated here.

$comment_builtins: Seven, and only because the record cannot carry them. FOUR were the builder's Kotlin catalog's alone and are published so a catalog-owned remote-m3 loses nothing, each transcribed from that catalog's definition (roles, traits, slots, properties and adapter notes verbatim): `remote-m3/remote-label-button` and `remote-m3/remote-material-theme` have call sites but no sticker here, and the builder writes both by id; `remote-m3/remote-time-text` has no sticker because the resolved writer rejects its DrawTextOnCircle opcode (see CatalogPreviews.kt); `remote-m3/lottie` is an asset player with no component call, filed under the builder's own `Content` shelf, which `menu.groupOrder` now carries. The label button's canvas adapter is claimed (`wear-m3/button`) but its slot mapping (`content` → `label`) is not expressible on a builtin yet. The other three are the widget containers. Of the containers, `remote-m3/widget-container-adaptive`, is EXPERIMENTAL: one widget authored once as named `headline` / `supporting` / `action` slots, which compose-ui-builder's `AdaptiveWearWidget.resolve` turns into the Small or Large container design before anything renders or exports it (Small drops `supporting`), so neither the device preview nor the generated source ever sees the adaptive id. It is declared here because a design rooted on it is otherwise refused by this catalog as an unknown component. The widget container is the Glance Wear HOST frame — the squircle the launcher draws around a widget, not a `remote-material3` component — so `WidgetContainerPreviews.kt` recreates it through `androidx.glance.wear`'s `WearWidgetPreview` wrapper and there is no component call for a record to find. That is exactly what a builtin is for: "it has no call site, so there is nothing to discover and no sticker to annotate". The containers matter more than two components' worth: this catalog's own policy says a Remote design starts from a container and everything else goes inside one, and the builder's record-free export routes on the ROOT component id — so a published catalog without these is one whose designs cannot be rooted. They were the blocker in https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/issues/674. `canvas: widget-container` is this catalog CLAIMING an adapter rather than a name anything validates: the Wasm canvas draws both by component id (UiBuilderRenderer's WearWidgetContainerScaffold), and a catalog claiming none would publish "not drawn on the canvas" about something the canvas draws. `remote-compose/document` stays out for the older reason: it is a BUILTIN OF THE BUILDER (https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_REMOTE_COMPOSE.md), and declaring it here would be this catalog claiming to own the builder's vocabulary.
$comment_remoteTextVocabulary: WHY remote-m3/remote-text STATES A VOCABULARY AND THE OTHER SEVEN DO NOT. A component that states none is published with the properties DERIVED from its signature, and the derivation keeps only what maps to a JSON scalar: `RemoteText` has twelve parameters and four survive — `text`, `color`, `fontSize`, `maxLines`. `style` is a `RemoteTextStyle` and `textAlign` a `TextAlign`, so both were dropped, and `style` is the parameter this component is actually set through: a design could size text and not scale it. What is stated here is additive — the same four, plus the two the derivation cannot see — and stops there, because a design may only set what the writer writes, and `RemoteContentEmitter` writes these six and the modifier — and, since compose-ui-builder#521, the text's `fontVariationSettings` and `fontFeatureSettings`, which every design system's text carries and which are stated here too. The four derived names are repeated verbatim rather than left to be merged, because a vocabulary is all-or-nothing per component: state one and it replaces the derivation entirely. ONE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MIGRATION: `style` is undeclared until this lands, so a stored value is tolerated and dropped from validation (https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/pull/840); once it is declared with `allowedValues`, a value outside the eighteen is INVALID rather than undeclared. Material 3 `headlineLarge`, `headlineMedium` and `headlineSmall` have no counterpart in this scale, so a design authored against the borrowed `m3/text` that carries one needs the role mapped by whatever rewrites it onto this component — the `supersedes` migration, not tolerance. Which Wear role each becomes is a design decision for this catalog and is deliberately not guessed here; publishing a `headline` role instead would publish one `RemoteTypography` cannot draw. The set is asserted against the compiled class by RemoteTextStyleVocabularyTest.
$comment_remoteIconVocabulary: remote-m3/remote-icon STATES ITS VOCABULARY for the reason remote-m3/remote-text's are: the derivation keeps only parameters that map to a JSON scalar, and `RemoteIcon`'s `imageVector` is an `ImageVector`, so the published component offered `contentDescription` and `tint` and no way to choose the glyph — every icon drew `addCircle`, and a launcher widget's icon buttons could not be expressed (https://github.com/yschimke/remote-m3-catalog/issues/12). The key is a Material icon key, the same vocabulary the canvas's `wear-m3/icon` reads as `iconKey` (mapped above, as `tint` is mapped onto the `color` that adapter reads) and the Browser Preview resolves through the renderer SDK's icon table. No `allowedValues`: the key table is the builder's, generated from material-icons-extended, and a copy here would be a second list to drift. The other two are repeated verbatim because a vocabulary is all-or-nothing per component.
$comment_components: Where a component sits on the shelf when the id it derives from does not say. One id per SYMBOL means a component lands on whichever catalog id sorts first: RemoteText is drawn by 29 stickers and arrived under Containment via AppCard, leaving the Text shelf empty. Canvas adapters are an approximate editing projection only: every one below is admitted by a `parallel` relationship to the sibling Wear catalog, while the authored properties and slots remain the Remote API's and the exported `.rc` Browser Preview plus generated Remote source remain authoritative. A canvasMapping translates only the names the Wear counterpart reads and never mutates the stored design or either export.

propertyCapabilities.name: text
propertyCapabilities.notes: The string the component draws. `RemoteText` takes a `RemoteString`, so a design's plain string is written as `"…".rs` and a binding or a state value as the remote expression it names — what the design carries is the same JSON either way.

propertyCapabilities.name: style
propertyCapabilities.notes: A role on this catalog's type scale, written as `style = RemoteMaterialTheme.typography.<role>`. This is the way to set type here: a role carries size, weight, line height and letter spacing together through `RemoteTextStyle`, which is why the catalog's own stickers pass a role OR an explicit size and never both. The eighteen are `RemoteTypography`'s own and are NOT the Material 3 fifteen — there is no `headline` on a watch, and there are five `numeral` roles a time or a metric is set in. A role this class does not have would export as a call that does not compile, so the list is exactly what it publishes.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontSize
propertyCapabilities.notes: Size in sp, as an override on top of `style` rather than a substitute for it — set it alone and everything else about the type comes from the ambient style. Spelled the parameter's own way; a design authored against the borrowed `m3/text` says `fontSizeSp` and the writer reads both. A whole number writes `22.rsp`; a fractional one writes `14.5f.sp.asRemoteTextUnit()`, because `RemoteTextUnitKt` publishes no `Float.rsp`.

propertyCapabilities.name: color
propertyCapabilities.notes: A colour: a `#RRGGBB` literal, which exports as `Color(0x…).rc`, or one of `colorTokens.roles`, which exports as `RemoteMaterialTheme.colorScheme.<role>`.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontVariationSettings
propertyCapabilities.notes: Variable-font axis coordinates, CSS `font-variation-settings` style with bare tags: `wght 650, wdth 87.5, GRAD -50`. Written as `RemoteText(fontVariationSettings = FontVariation.Settings(…))`, so the document carries the axes and the player applies them to the face it resolves; an axis that face does not have is ignored. `wght` set here overrides `fontWeight`.

propertyCapabilities.name: fontFeatureSettings
propertyCapabilities.notes: OpenType layout features, CSS `font-feature-settings` style with bare tags: `tnum, ss01, liga 0`. Written as `style = ….merge(fontFeatureSettings = …)`, since `RemoteText` has no feature parameter; Remote Compose carries them in the document beside the axes. A feature the typeface does not have is ignored.

propertyCapabilities.name: imageVector
propertyCapabilities.notes: A Material icon key (`home`, `search`, `addCircle`, …), written as `Icons.<Style>.<Name>.toRemoteImageVector()` — `RemoteIcon` takes a `RemoteImageVector` captured from the `androidx.compose.material.icons` vector. Unset draws `addCircle`, the default the canvas mapping above gives.

propertyCapabilities.name: contentDescription
propertyCapabilities.notes: What a screen reader says for the icon. Leave it empty beside a label; set it when the icon is the whole button.

propertyCapabilities.name: tint
propertyCapabilities.notes: A colour: a `#RRGGBB` literal or one of `colorTokens.roles`. Unset inherits the enclosing content colour, which is how a button's colour reaches its icon.

propertyCapabilities.name: pageCount
propertyCapabilities.notes: How many pages there are; 4 when absent. `state` is a `RemotePageIndicatorState`, which no design value becomes, so the emitter builds it from this and `selectedPage`.

propertyCapabilities.name: selectedPage
propertyCapabilities.notes: The page shown, from zero: a literal or the design's Int state, which is how a pager drives the dots. The first when absent.

propertyCapabilities.name: pageCount
propertyCapabilities.notes: How many pages there are; 4 when absent. `state` is a `RemotePageIndicatorState`, which no design value becomes, so the emitter builds it from this and `selectedPage`.

The canvas has no Lottie renderer, and compiling the animation the way the export does — into Remote Compose operations — is Horologist's Android-only creation API, which a Wasm build cannot link. $comment_templates: The five template designs this module offers in the New design chooser, as branch-relative paths the design-artifacts pipeline copies from remote-catalog/ui-builder/designs/ onto the delivery branch beside ui-builder.json. Transcribed from the Kotlin builders in compose-ui-builder's UiBuilderTemplates.kt, which remain the live seed until the server reads this entry (SEED_TEMPLATES step 5): the two host frames whose dimensions THIS FILE already declares in frame.geometry.sizesDp, the EXPERIMENTAL adaptive widget (AdaptiveWearWidget.newDocument, authored at the Large frame it edits at; the builder resolves it to Small or Large before rendering or exporting), and the two worked designs reproducing android/wear-os-samples' WearWidget sample. Hand-authored designs rather than vendored bytes, so the `groups` exception for :samples-catalog does not apply to them. The chooser's per-template label, supporting text, order and default are NOT expressible in the schema yet (SEED_TEMPLATES step 3, compose-ai-tools): wear-widget-small 'Wear widget · Small (216×76dp)', wear-widget-large 'Wear widget · Large (216×124dp)', wear-widget-adaptive 'Wear widget · Adaptive (experimental)', hello-widget 'Hello widget' (default), weather-widget 'Weather widget'. Each document pins `environment.fixedTime` to 2024-05-16T12:00:00Z, the instant the Kotlin seeds use, so a render never reads the system clock. Each document's `catalogPin` is the placeholder the server rewrites at creation, never a live revision. The round trip they need — document to generated creation-DSL Kotlin, compiled against this module's own alpha Remote trio — is WidgetTemplateRoundTripTest, the gate only this repository can run. See docs/UI_BUILDER_TEMPLATES.md and https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_SEED_TEMPLATES.md
$comment_supersedes: The builder's Kotlin remote-m3 catalog borrows Material 3's `m3/text` beside this catalog's own `remote-m3/remote-text`; the published catalog has only the Remote one, which is the text a Remote document can actually write (PublishedRemoteM3CatalogEquivalenceTest). A saved design carrying `m3/text` is migrated onto it rather than stranded. `fontSizeSp` is the one property spelled differently (`fontSize` here, as the canvas mapping already says); every other name carries over, and one `remote-text` does not declare (`fontWeight`, `fontStyle`, `lineHeightSp`, …) is reported by the upgrade preview rather than silently dropped. Material 3's headline styles have no counterpart in `remote-text`'s Wear scale (see $comment_remoteTextVocabulary): a migrated design carrying one is reported invalid, and which Wear role each becomes stays a design decision.
$comment_code: No `code` block yet, so the export stays `record`. A Remote widget is written in the creation DSL rather than in Compose, which is a `code.language` and a set of structural templates — and both arrive with the template engine, not ahead of it. Until then the export prints call sites from the record, which is what it already does.
